name: Pickaxes (the whole family)
change: Eight tiers, one per ore: wooden, stone, copper, bronze, iron, steel, cobalt steel, tungsten steel. The silver, gold and platinum pickaxes become the bronze, cobalt-steel and tungsten-steel ones. The rock drill (powered, tungsten-steel bits) joins the top tier as the faster option, never the only way to reach an ore.
reason: Every pickaxe tier opens a new ore, so none is skippable (P20, P21). Copper and bronze both stay: each opens its own ore, and both outfits are made (D69).

name: Axes (the whole family)
change: Three axes, then two special tools: the stone axe (the first, for ordinary trees), the iron axe (hardwood too) and the steel axe (faster on both); the saw, much faster than any axe on big trees; and the chainsaw at the top (powered, fast on every tree). The wooden, copper, silver and gold axes go; the platinum axe becomes the chainsaw.
reason: Trees come in two kinds of wood, ordinary and hard, each with big trees, so the axe needs only a few steps (P21, D69).

name: Shovels (the whole family)
change: Three tiers: wooden, copper, iron. Each takes one hit fewer per square at the same swing speed (three, two, then one) on dirt blocks and ground alike. The stone, steel, silver, gold and platinum shovels go. The shovel does all three jobs from the start: digging dirt blocks, digging up ground and laying ground, on the square the player points at, within reach. Past iron, the power spade is the faster step.
reason: Digging is an early-game skill that tops out a few sessions in, so it never becomes a chore; tool lines may finish at different speeds (D69).

name: Hoes (the whole family)
change: Three tiers: wooden, copper, iron, covering one square, then up to two by two, then up to three by three. R picks the size, up to the tool's largest, and the cursor outlines the squares first, so a single square is always possible. The stone, steel, silver, gold and platinum hoes go. Playtesting confirms the sizes.
reason: Farm tools improve by area, not speed, stay few and aren't locked behind late metals (P21, D12, D69).

name: Scythes (the whole family)
change: Three tiers: wooden, copper, iron, reaping one square, then up to two by two, then up to three by three, picked with R like the hoe; only ripe crops are cut. The steel, silver, gold and platinum scythes go. The harvest sickle leaves the farm line and becomes the bug-part mandible sickle. Playtesting confirms the sizes.
reason: The same rule as the hoe (D69); today all seven scythes reap the same three-by-three patch, so the extra tiers add nothing.

name: Nets (the whole family)
change: The small and large hand nets and the cast net; no metal tiers. The small net takes a few small bugs at a time; the large one takes more flies per swing and bigger bugs such as wasps. Which nets can hold a bug is set per species: examining a bug says at once which nets can't, and its other facts (the bait it likes, what it needs to breed) open as the player examines more of that species. The cast net is thrown over a big bug and holds it still briefly so it can be dragged; it never stays in the world (the placed trap is the net that stays put).
reason: Hand nets are split by bug size; bigger bugs go to placed catchers, dragging and the cast net (P3, P15, D12, D69).

name: Watering cans (the whole family)
reason: Small and large only (D12); later watering comes from sprinklers and the hand pump (P22), not bigger cans.

name: Swords (the whole family)
change: Wooden, copper, bronze, iron, steel; past steel the black-ant jaw blade, then the fire-ant jaw blade. The silver, gold and platinum swords go.
reason: Weapons climb the tool metals to steel, and past steel the best blades come from zinc-hardened bug jaws (P20).

name: Spears (the whole family)
change: Wooden, copper, bronze, iron, steel; past steel the scorpion-sting spear. The silver, gold and platinum spears go, and so do both harpoons.
reason: Same ladder as the sword; a scorpion's sting tip is up to a quarter zinc, which makes it the natural spear point past steel (P20).

name: Daggers (the whole family)
change: Copper, bronze, iron, steel (no wooden dagger); past steel the centipede-fang dagger, then the spider-fang dagger. The silver, gold and platinum daggers go.
reason: A fast, short weapon for agility and stealth players is the attack-speed style D16 asks for beside knockback, and fangs are real zinc-hardened daggers.

name: Maces (the whole family)
change: Copper, bronze, iron, steel maces, then the Rhino-Horn Maul past steel: slow, heavy swings that knock bugs back and hit hard-shelled bugs (beetles, pill bugs, crabs) harder. The club merges in; no wooden or precious-metal maces.
reason: Gives the tank a weapon of its own with knockback (D16), climbing to a boss-horn top like every other line.

name: Clubs (the whole family)
reason: A club is a cheaper mace doing the same job; the mace family covers it.

name: Bows (the whole family)
reason: Ranged weapons are set aside (D12); if they come back, one bow gets designed then, not a metal ladder of them.

name: Armour ladder (the whole family)
change: Worn whole, one outfit at a time (D47): bug leather and padded cloth, then copper, bronze, iron, steel and cobalt-steel outfits; platinum only in the fancy platinum plate, which also needs steel; gold only as gilding (the gilded-steel outfit). Today's single pieces (caps, boots, chests and so on) merge into their outfit. Silver and gold leave the ladder.
reason: Armour follows the tool metals (P20, D61), and outfits have no pieces (D47).

name: Accessories (the whole family)
change: Keep only accessories that do one real, visible thing no outfit, weapon or potion already does: the prospector's loupe, the headlamp (from the flashlight), the UV lamp, the red-light lamp, polarised glasses, the colony-scent pouch, the mosquito head net, and four more for the roles with none: the running brace (agility), the seed spreader (farming), the hunter's field guide (attack) and the medic's satchel (tank and support). Cut every luck piece, every stat ring and every set band. Beekeepers need none: the bee-suit line and the three smokers are their gear.
reason: Two slots should hold a choice between clever objects, and every role should find at least one (the 2026-08-06 rule that each role has its own best gear).

reason: Platinum is about as soft as copper and very heavy (P20); tungsten steel is a real tool steel with a name players know (D69).

reason: The top tiers include power tools (P21, D69); no existing item can become it, since the platinum pick becomes the tungsten-steel pick.

name: Poison Vial

name: Pollen Loaf
change: Merge into the Pollen Patty (the renamed bee bread)

name: Pollination Dust

name: Pollinators Loaf
reason: It repeats the roast's farming boost, and pollination is the bees' job.

name: Poppy
reason: The red dye (the only red source) and a common village flower (294 placed).

name: Propolis Salve
change: Becomes the Honey Bandage: cloth plus honey; it heals over a few seconds, one at a time, and can be used on a friend (P16, P17).
reason: Honey dressings and propolis are real wound treatments, and this was the old list's first heal-over-time item.

name: Reeds
change: Drop fibre instead of 'reeds', which has no item and no use (D15 folds reed fibre into fibre).
reason: The waterside plant stays (235 placed); dragonfly young really climb reeds to become adults, so it is their habitat.

name: Regen Tonic
reason: Healing over time is what meals and bandages do.

name: Royal Jelly Tonic
change: The premium health meal: royal jelly from the bees (ants don't make royal jelly) plus honey; its one boost is the biggest health pool. The royal tonic folds into it.
reason: Royal jelly is a signature ingredient and deserves a top dish.

name: Royal Tonic
change: Merge into the Royal Jelly Tonic
reason: The same royal jelly and honey health boost, as a potion; a bigger health pool is a meal's job.

name: Rubble
reason: Broken stone from the old world, and a stone source (166 placed).

name: Sage
reason: A cooking herb in three kept meals (the roast, the warrior's breakfast, the forager's stew); it sits in no real zone yet, so it needs placing.

name: Pumpkin Seeds
reason: Sold at the General Store, and the harvest sometimes gives more (D24).

name: Tomato Seeds
reason: Sold at the General Store and in the starting bag; the harvest sometimes gives more (D24).

name: Wheat Seeds

reason: Wheat seeds are bought or harvested in the Locust Farmland (D42).

name: Serpent Elixir
reason: Made from an invented 'serpent fly', and it mixes boosts that other items already give.

name: Silk Tea Biscuit
reason: A general calming boost; calming is set species by species (D35).

name: Smoke Bomb
reason: Smoke calms bees, which the bee smoker already does, and general calming goes.

name: Snail Skewer
reason: There are no snails (D64).

name: Speed Noodles

name: Spider Antivenom
change: merge into antivenom
reason: Spider bites are venom; a stronger spider gives a stronger strength.

name: Spider Jerky
change: Merge into the Bug Jerky
reason: The same trail food; spider is one of the bug meats it takes (fried spider is a real dish).

name: Standing Stone
reason: A landmark (26 placed); it should stop swaying in the wind, as D60 notes.

name: Steady Hand Tea
reason: The one catching meal (a wider, steadier net swing), early and cheap; chamomile, a real calming tea, fits its recipe.

name: Still Mind Incense
reason: General calming (P16, D35).

name: Tree Stump
reason: What is left of a felled tree: wood, and a real shelter for beetles.

name: Sunflower
change: Harvesting gives sunflower seeds, which also replant it (the one harvest rule, D24); make it a nectar and pollen plant that bees feed on.
reason: A real bee plant and seed crop that adds farming variety; only 14 are placed now.

name: Swarm Lure
reason: Bait in a dish already draws bugs to a spot (P4).

name: Swarm Repellent
reason: Making every swarm bug keep away is general calming by another name (D35).

name: Swarm Repeller
reason: Made for army ants, a species that is cut (D39).

name: Swift Tonic
reason: Walking speed is the garden salad's job, and potions only do what food can't.

name: Tall Grass
reason: The main fibre source and the commonest greenery (2,174 placed); home ground for grasshoppers and crickets.

name: Thorns Draught
reason: Hurting attackers is the thorn outfits' job (three tiers, August 2026).

name: Thyme
reason: A cooking herb in two kept meals (the angler's supper, the steady-hand tea) and a real bee plant; it sits in no real zone yet, so it needs placing.

name: Tick Repellent
change: Rename 'Tick Repellent': ticks can't latch on for a while. Keep (later), for the desert zone's ticks; mosquitoes are the head net's job.
reason: A head net guards the face from flying biters but can't stop ticks climbing up from the ground, so each item gets its own bug; ticks count as bugs (D64).

name: Torchlight Brew
change: Merge into the Night Sight Potion
reason: Another night-sight brew; P16 makes them one potion.

name: Apple Tree

name: Cherry Tree

name: Dead Tree

name: Fruit Tree
reason: A plain copy of the apple tree that doesn't even bear fruit, placed in no real zone.

name: Oak Tree
reason: The standard wood tree (1,774 placed).

reason: A fruit tree (14 placed), part of the orchard's variety.

reason: A health-pool boost the royal jelly meal already gives; a bigger health pool is a meal's job.

name: Warden Stew
reason: A second defence meal (the crayfish boil is the one), and hurting attackers is the thorn outfits' job.

name: Warding Tonic
reason: Heat, cold and spore hazards don't exist in the game.

name: Warriors Breakfast
change: One boost only: harder hits (more attack damage); drop the defence half. It takes any bug meat; The crit skewer and the fried locust fold into it.
reason: It is early and cheap (corn, sage, bug meat), and the set needs one attack meal.

name: Wasp Nest
reason: The wasps' nursery, already built.

name: Water Breathing Potion
reason: Water breathing (no diving), and it needs leeches.

name: Water Lily
reason: A second lily pad that only gives fibre and sits in no real zone; the lily pad covers it.

name: Widow Antivenom
change: merge into antivenom
reason: Black-widow venom makes the strongest antivenom (stronger bugs, stronger potions, P16).

name: Widow Bomb
change: Merge into the Bug Bomb (the renamed poison vial)
reason: The strongest strength; insecticides made from spider venom are real.

name: Wild Berry Bush
change: Picking takes the berries and leaves the bush to fruit again; cutting it down gives fibre (P11).
reason: Today one hit removes the bush for a single berry, but bushes are meant to keep producing (P11).

name: Wildflower Honey Toast
reason: It only heals, and the honey cake covers honey baking.

name: Woodland Tonic
reason: A mix of health and night-sight boosts that the meals and the night-sight potion cover.

name: Yarrow
reason: The healing potion's herb (yarrow is a real traditional wound herb); common in the village (138 placed).

name: Venom Resistance Potion
change: A potion that makes venom do less harm for a few minutes, with no wait; made from bug venom, stronger when it comes from stronger bugs (P16).
reason: P16's starting set names it, and no old item does it on its own (the old cures only had short resistance tacked on).

name: Cloth Bandage
change: Made from cloth; heals a little over a few seconds, one at a time; hold it and left-click a friend to heal them (P16, P17).
reason: The cheapest heal, available as soon as the player has cloth.

name: Chitin Bandage
change: Cloth plus chitin from the bug extractor; the strongest bandage (the honey bandage, made from the propolis salve, sits between).
reason: Chitin-based wound dressings are real, and it ties bandages to bug farming (P16).

name: Bug Meat
change: The bug extractor turns a carcass into bug meat, the ingredient every bug-meat meal takes (hearty stew, warrior's breakfast, bug jerky).
reason: The overview promises 'meat from carcasses' and D18 says the extractor feeds cooking, but no meat item exists, and big carcasses are dragged rather than bagged (P15).

name: Straw
change: Comes from cutting wheat down (P11); used for the straw bale, mulch, a straw beehive, a straw hat and compost.
reason: Five things are made from straw (P11, D66), but no straw item exists.

name: Flour
change: The mill turns wheat into flour in one step (P11); the honey cake and the honeydew bun need it.
reason: P11 names the mill's flour, and no flour item exists.

name: Milkweed Seed
change: Sometimes dropped when milkweed is harvested or cut (D23, D24), and sold; grows a new milkweed, which is a new butterfly nursery.
reason: Butterfly farmers need a way to grow nurseries, and D24 names this seed.

name: Wildflower Seeds
change: Sometimes dropped by the coloured wildflowers (D24), and sold; grows one of the nectar flowers bees and butterflies feed on.
reason: Bee and butterfly farmers need to plant flowers, and D24 names this seed.

name: Herb and flower seeds (one per plant)
change: One seed item for each kept herb and dye flower (yarrow, aloe, lavender, chamomile, clover, dandelion, poppy, mint, sage, thyme, agave), sometimes dropped at harvest (D24) and sold by a townsperson.
reason: The one harvest rule needs a seed for every plant, but only the seven crops have one; potion and bee gardens depend on them.

name: Tree saplings (one per tree)
change: One sapling for each kept tree (apple, orange, plum, cherry, oak, pine, palm), sometimes dropped when a tree is chopped (D24); fruit-tree saplings are also sold.
reason: Players can't replant trees or plant an orchard today, and D24 says trees give saplings.

name: Acid Crystal
reason: A 'corrosive gem' is not a real mineral, and nothing needs it once fire and acid gear is gone (P2).

name: Albino Chitin
change: merge into chitin: the pale cave isopod gives ordinary chitin at the bug extractor.
reason: A white plate that does chitin's job under another name; one chitin item is enough for the plain shells.

name: Aloe Leaf
change: Merge into aloe (the herb kept as the burn salve's base).
reason: The same plant twice: aloe already exists as its own item, and it is the salve's main ingredient.

name: Amber Dye
reason: A second orange-yellow dye made from a butterfly wing; more colours should come from flowers at the dye station (P11), and butterfly scales are cut.

name: Ant Egg
reason: The item the ant nursery gives when you take its brood, as wasp larvae come from the wasp nest, so ant ranchers can start a colony of their own (D67); the myrmecologist can trade it.

name: Ant Fungus
reason: Our two ants, black and fire ants, don't farm fungus.

name: Aphid Cluster
reason: Aphids are tiny bugs living on plants, seen in the plant's own view (part 8), and a killed bug drops only its carcass (D18); honeydew is the aphids' useful product.

name: Apple
reason: Fruit from the apple trees (81 trees placed): food, juice at the press (P11), and the rotting fruit flies breed on.

name: Aquatic Grub
reason: Fishing bait comes from bug meat and caught bugs, so a separate grub drop adds nothing, and bugs drop only carcasses (D18).

name: Fire Ant Jaw
change: Rename 'Fire Ant Jaw': taken from dead fire ants at the bug extractor (best from older ants), in the Deadly Ants zone; it edges the Fire-Ant Jaw Blade, the top bug-part sword.
reason: Army ants are cut (two ant species, D39), but the fire-ant blade this table keeps needs fire-ant jaws from this same zone (P20).

name: Bark Beetle Jaw
reason: The stag beetle's jaw is the one beetle jaw with a job (the mandible sickle); bark beetles give chitin like other beetles.

name: Bark Strip
reason: Its jobs were tanning hides and bark medicines, and neither exists: there are no mammal hides, and tanning is an extra realistic step the game skips (D42).

name: Bat Guano
reason: There are no bats (D32); compost is the fertiliser.

name: Beeswax
reason: Made at the honey extractor from honeycomb; candles and the burn salve's base use it, and the Beekeeper buys it.

name: Beeswax Dab
change: merge into beeswax
reason: Wild wax picked up in the village is the same wax; D19 already moved it out of the village, and hives are where wax comes from.

name: Beetle Air Sac
reason: It was a water-breathing ingredient, and there is no diving (August 2026).

name: Beetle Carapace
change: merge into chitin
reason: Stag and rhino beetle shells are beetle chitin, which the bug extractor already makes from dead beetles.

name: Crop Beetle Mandible
reason: Its job was the harvest sickle's edge, which the stag beetle's jaw now takes (the Mandible Sickle); one beetle jaw is enough.

name: Wild Berries
reason: The wild berry bush's fruit, picked again and again once the bush keeps producing (P11); food and juice.

name: Black Silt
reason: Dredged mud for a special swamp brick; one kind of rock and a few building materials are enough (D22), and dredging is only a backlog idea (D14).

name: Blighted Grain
reason: Invented 'blighted' grain; locust swarms simply eat the wheat (D63), and the porridge made from it is cut.

name: Blind Beetle Shell
change: merge into chitin
reason: A cave beetle's shell is ordinary beetle chitin.

name: Blind Fish Scale
reason: It fed luck charms, which are cut; fish are caught whole with a rod.

name: Blue Dye
reason: One of the four basic dyes, made at the dye station and sold by the Weaver; dyes recolour cloth outfits (D44).

name: Bog Iron
change: Merge into iron ore: swamp iron deposits simply give iron ore.
reason: Bog iron is real, but a second iron ore does the same job; one ore per rung keeps the ladder clear (P20).

name: Bog Pearl
reason: Its jobs were luck charms and diving, both cut, and mussels, being molluscs, didn't survive (D32, D64).

name: Bogwood Plank
reason: A swamp plank from sunken logs that needs diving or dredging; planks and hardwood cover building.

name: Bone
change: New job: the mill grinds bones into bone meal, a fertiliser (see the bone meal row); bone piles keep dropping it.
reason: Old remains stay (D66), and grinding bones into fertiliser is real and a proven game idea (Stardew's bone mill), which gives the bone piles a reason to be broken.

name: Bored Bark
reason: Beetle-chewed bark as a drop from a killed bug (D18 rules those out), for invented bark medicines.

name: Boulder
reason: Rocks and boulders were retired three times: the stone block is the one rock (D22); it is placed in no real zone.

name: Bramble Vine
reason: The bramble is cut, and thorn armour comes from real stings (the thorn outfits), not woven thorns (D10).

name: Brick
change: Fire bricks from clay blocks at the furnace instead of cutting them from stone blocks at the stonecutter; stone keeps its own walls.
reason: Real brick is fired clay, and this gives clay its one job; the brick walls and the Stonemason's stock stay as they are.

name: Bronze Bar
reason: The fourth rung of the metal ladder (P20): copper bars and washed tin ore at the forge; bronze tools, weapons and armour, and the Blacksmith sells it.

name: Broodmother Silk
change: Keep as the Spider Vale brood-mother's own part (the biggest female of the vale's hunting spider): only her carcass gives it, and it goes into a recipe from the Ecologist's quests (P9, P13).
reason: Female spiders are usually much bigger than males, so a brood-mother boss is real biology, and P13 promises each boss a material of its own.

name: Bullet Ant Stinger
reason: Bullet ants are cut (two ant species, D39), and the dagger made from it is cut.

name: Bumble Fuzz
reason: Bee fuzz for linings and brushes has no real use; cloth and fibre cover padding.

name: Bumble Nectar
reason: Bumblebees store only a little nectar, and honey from the hive already fills this role.

name: Butterfly Press
reason: A mounted butterfly repeats the specimen case, which already displays bugs (two placed).

name: Butterfly Scale
reason: Its jobs were luck charms and a shimmering dye, and a shimmer can't be made by recolouring (dyes recolour cloth outfits, D44); dead butterflies give bug leather.

name: Cabbage
reason: A village vegetable (D19) used in the kept meals; cabbage whites really lay their eggs on it.

name: Cabbage Caterpillar
reason: Caterpillars are living bugs that grow up in the world (D38), not an item; a killed bug drops only its carcass (D18).

name: Camel Cricket Leg
reason: Its job was springy boots for fall damage, and a world seen from above has no falls; crickets give chitin and bug meat.

name: Carpenter Resin
reason: Carpenter bees bore wood, they don't make resin; tree resin covers sealing and coatings.

name: Carrot
reason: A village vegetable (D19) and a staple of the kept meals.

name: Cattail Fluff
change: merge into fiber
reason: Cattails now drop plain fibre, and D15 folds water-plant fibres into fibre.

name: Cave Beetle Carapace
change: merge into chitin
reason: A cave beetle's wing-case is ordinary beetle chitin.

name: Cave Crab Carapace
change: merge into chitin
reason: Crabs count as bugs (D64) and their shell is chitin; the diving set it was for is gone.

name: Cave Crystal Geode
change: Merge into the geode (the mining find the gem cutter cracks open)
reason: A second geode doing the same job in another zone.

name: Cave Detritus
reason: Rotting cave litter as a drop from a killed bug, which D18 rules out; compost and leaf litter cover decomposer food.

name: Cave Nettle
reason: A counter-irritant for an old cure; the antivenom is made from venom (P16), and nettles don't grow in the dark.

name: Cave Nitre
reason: Its jobs were preserving, gem etching and gunpowder, and none exists: salt cures food, the gem cutter needs nothing extra, and dynamite isn't designed.

name: Cave Pearl
reason: Its jobs were luck and diving charms, both cut; real cave pearls are stone balls that grow in dripping pools, so one could return as a rare cave find if wanted.

name: Cave Quartz
change: merge into quartz
reason: The same mineral under a second name for other zones.

name: Cave River Dye
reason: A zone 'palette' of dyes; the dye station makes single colours from plants (P11), not a set per zone.

name: Cave Salt
change: Merge into Salt (the renamed rock salt)
reason: Salt is salt; one item serves the bug jerky and the crayfish boil.

name: Cave Spider Silk
reason: The first of three spider silks (cave spider, spider, black widow), for the cave-spider silk outfit, the stealth line's first tier; from cave spiders at the bug extractor, which live in the lower underground (D21).

name: Cave Water
reason: Water isn't an item, and the cold-water brews it fed are cut.

name: Cavern Dye
reason: A zone dye palette; single plant dyes cover colour (P11).

name: Centipede Parts
reason: A vague leftover drop that D22 removed; nothing makes or uses it, and centipedes give chitin, fangs and venom at the bug extractor.

name: Centipede Plate
change: merge into chitin
reason: A centipede's plates are ordinary chitin, which dead centipedes already give.

name: Centipede Venom
reason: The third of six venoms (wasp, hornet, centipede, scorpion, spider, black widow): from the big hunting centipedes at the bug extractor; the antivenom, venom resistance and the venom coating take it, stronger bugs making stronger potions (P16).

name: Centipede Venom Gland
change: Merge into centipede venom
reason: The same centipede venom under a second name.

name: Chalk Stone
reason: A second stone; the ant zones are dirt (D43) and there is one kind of rock (D22).

name: Charcoal
change: merge into coal: the furnace burns wood into coal, as Stardew's charcoal kiln does.
reason: It does coal's job under another name; the wood route matters because the village needs coal for torches and glass before the player reaches the mines.

name: Cherry
reason: Fruit from the cherry trees (30 trees placed), part of the orchard's variety; food, juice and fly food when it rots.

name: Chitin
reason: The common bug plate the bug extractor already makes from dead beetles (fastest), wasps, centipedes and millipedes; the beetle-shell outfit and the chitin bandage use it, and seventeen zone shells fold into it.

name: Chitin Weave
reason: A cloth woven from beetle shell and locust wings for the cut locust set (D10).

name: Cicada Shell
change: merge into chitin
reason: A cicada's shell is chitin; the springy-armour job it had doesn't exist.

name: Cicada Wing
reason: Its jobs were a gliding trinket and inlay, and there is nothing to glide over in a world seen from above.

name: Clay
change: Merge into the clay block: the clay block is the one clay item, and the furnace fires it into bricks.
reason: Blocks drop themselves (D22), so a loose clay item and a clay block would be the same material twice.

name: Cloth
reason: Woven from thread at the loom and sold by the Weaver; beds, sofas, bandages and cloth outfits use it.

name: Clover Honey
change: merge into honey
reason: One honey item is the signature ingredient; a honey per flower would multiply items for little play.

name: Coal
reason: Fuel for the furnace and forge, torches and steel; mined underground, and the furnace also makes it from wood once charcoal folds in.

name: Cobweb
change: Merge into spider silk: cutting a web with a blade gives spider silk (D12).
reason: Raw web is spider silk; D12 already says webbing is cut for silk.

name: Cold Iron Ore
reason: 'Cold iron' is fairy-tale iron (P2), and a second iron ore adds nothing.

name: Comb Foundation
reason: A wax sheet for hive frames is an extra realistic beekeeping step (D42); hives make comb by themselves.

name: Compost
reason: Made in the compost bin while flies breed in it; it sells and is a fertiliser (D37).

name: Rich Compost
change: merge into compost
reason: D19 already folded it into plain compost: one type.

name: Copper Bar
reason: The third rung of the metal ladder (P20): the first metal tools, weapons and armour, and half of bronze; the Blacksmith sells it.

name: Copper Ore
reason: The first metal ore, reached with the stone pickaxe (P20); crushed, washed, then smelted (D26).

name: Crushed Copper Ore
change: Rename 'Crushed Copper Ore' (the rock crusher's output); the step stays.
reason: The owner chose crush, wash, smelt (D26), and D13 marked 'paydirt' as a working name; 'crushed ore' says what it is.

name: Corn
reason: A village vegetable (238 plants placed) used in the roast and the warrior's breakfast; cut stalks go to compost (P11).

name: Crab Claw
reason: A weapon part with no weapon (no crab weapon is kept); crabs give chitin and bug meat.

name: Crayfish Claw
reason: The crayfish boil cooks crayfish whole, and bugs drop only carcasses (D18).

name: Crayfish Shell
change: merge into chitin
reason: Crayfish count as bugs (D64), and their shell is chitin; the diving gear it was for is gone.

name: Cricket Song Organ
reason: Its jobs were a swarm lure and a charm, both cut; crickets give chitin and bug meat.

name: Crop Beetle Shell
change: merge into chitin
reason: Beetle shell is chitin; the locust-warden armour it plated is cut (D10).

name: Crystal
change: Merge into quartz: the crystal clusters drop quartz.
reason: The clusters are quartz crystals already, and two names for one mineral confuse; quartz is the real name and has the gem cutter's recipe.

name: Cut Diamond
reason: The gem cutter turns a diamond into a stone worth far more, for selling and jewelry; diamonds make no tools (D49).

name: Cut Emerald
reason: A cut gem for selling and jewelry, one simple step at the gem cutter.

name: Cut Glow Crystal
reason: Crystals don't glow by themselves; light comes from bugs, torches and lamps (D49).

name: Cut Glowquartz
reason: Quartz that lights itself would be magic, and it needed formic etch, which is cut.

name: Cut Quartz
reason: The cheap cut gem, a first jewelry stone and a small step up in value from common quartz.

name: Cut Ruby
reason: A cut gem for selling and jewelry.

name: Cut Sapphire
reason: A cut gem for selling and jewelry.

name: Damselfly Wing
reason: Its jobs were a gliding pin and gossamer cloth, both cut; damselflies give chitin and bug meat.

name: Dead Ant
change: Becomes the black ant's carcass ('Dead Black Ant'); fire ants get a carcass of their own when they are built, so the bug extractor can give each ant its own chitin and jaw. Only black ants give formic acid; fire ants don't make it (their sting is a different venom, which the antivenom treats).
reason: The two ant outfits and the two jaw blades come from different ants, and the examine text will teach that only some ants make formic acid.

name: Dead Bee
change: Give it bug extractor recipes: chitin and bug meat.
reason: Every carcass should become something at the extractor (D18); today a dead bee only feeds the compost bin.

name: Dead Beetle
reason: The bug extractor turns it into chitin fastest, which makes beetles the beetle-shell outfit's source; left on the ground it feeds the carrion beetles.

name: Dead Butterfly
reason: The bug extractor turns it into bug leather, as the owner's bug map (2026-06-28) says.

name: Dead Centipede
change: Besides chitin, a big centipede's carcass also gives a centipede fang or centipede venom, each its own extractor recipe so the player chooses what the carcass becomes (as honeycomb gives honey or wax, D31).
reason: The centipede-fang dagger and the centipede venom need a source, and D18 says it is the extractor.

name: Dead Dragonfly
change: Give it bug extractor recipes: chitin and bug meat.
reason: Dragonflies are kept (the wasps' counterweight), but their carcass becomes nothing today.

name: Dead Firefly
change: Give it bug extractor recipes: the glow gland (while the glowworm armour stays on the roster) and bug meat.
reason: Its carcass becomes nothing today, and the firefly is the village's night bug (P23).

name: Dead Fly
reason: The first carcass most players get; the bug extractor turns it into bug leather for the starting outfit.

name: Dead Millipede
reason: The bug extractor turns it into chitin; millipedes count as bugs (D64).

name: Dead Wasp
change: Besides chitin, a dead wasp also gives a wasp stinger or wasp venom, each its own extractor recipe so the player chooses (as with honeycomb, D31).
reason: The wasp-thorn outfit and the first antivenom need these, and D18 routes every bug part through the extractor.

name: Deep Swamp Dye
reason: A zone dye palette built on an invented 'serpent' glow; single plant dyes cover colour (P11).

name: Deepwater Kelp
reason: Gathered by diving (out), and kelp is a sea plant, not a swamp one.

name: Defensive Toxin
reason: The millipede's spray is a hazard the burn salve treats, not an ingredient; millipedes give chitin.

name: Desert Sand
change: Merge into the sand block
reason: Sand is sand; one sand item makes glass wherever it is dug.

name: Diamond
reason: The top gem from the deepest deposits; it sells and cuts into a jewelry stone, and makes no tools (D49).

name: Dirt
change: Merge into the dirt block: one dirt item, placed as a block from the hotbar and laid as ground by the shovel.
reason: Digging dirt ground gives 'dirt' while breaking a dirt block gives 'dirt block', so dirt dug in the ant zones can't be laid as ground; blocks drop themselves (D22).

name: Dragonfly Eye
reason: Its job was a night-sight lens, and seeing in the dark is the potion's job (D54).

name: Dragonfly Wing
reason: Its jobs were a glider and gossamer cloth, both cut.

name: Dripstone
reason: A second cave stone; one kind of rock (D22).

name: Duckweed Paste
reason: A green dye and fertiliser additive from a plant no zone has; green dye and compost already exist.

name: Dust Lichen
reason: Its jobs were a glue and the old tick repellent's filler, neither kept.

name: Earwig Pincer
reason: A combat drop with no recipe; earwigs give chitin and bug meat.

name: Egg Sac
reason: Brood of an invented spiderling swarm; a nursery's young are taken from the nursery itself, not dropped.

name: Eggplant
reason: A village vegetable with several harvests; its seed needs a seller (see the eggplant seeds).

name: Elite Chitin
reason: A refined plate made by forging chitin, a realistic extra step (D42) for the cut fire-warden set; the fire-ant outfit uses fire ant chitin directly.

name: Ember Resin
reason: A fire glue for fire weapons and fire armour; fire ants sting rather than burn, and fire isn't a hazard in the game.

name: Emerald
reason: A gem mined from emerald deposits; it sells and cuts into a jewelry stone.

name: Emperor Moth Silk
change: merge into silk
reason: Emperor moths are real wild silk moths, but their silk is the same moth silk as the rest.

name: Eyespot Scale
reason: Its job was a dodge trinket, and dodging belongs to the player's own move (P14).

name: Plant Fiber
reason: The common cordage from grass, bushes, reeds and cattails (D15); spun into thread, and reed and water-plant fibres fold into it.

name: Fire Ant Gland
reason: Fire ants sting, they don't make fire, and fire isn't a hazard; fire ants give chitin, jaws and formic acid.

name: Firefly Dust
reason: A second glow powder from the same bug; one glow material is enough.

name: Glow Gland
change: Rename 'Glow Gland': the one glow material, from dead fireflies and glowworms at the bug extractor; its job is the glowworm armour on the outfit roster (armour made from glowworm light). If that outfit is dropped, this goes with it.
reason: Lanterns hold live fireflies and glowworms (D12, D21), so a glow material earns its place only as the light outfit's material; two other glow items merge into it and the rest of the glow pile is cut.

name: Fish Fillet
reason: Fish are caught whole with a rod and cooked whole (the angler's supper takes village fish).

name: Flame Alloy
reason: A fire-tempered fantasy metal (P2); past steel the ladder is cobalt steel and tungsten steel (P20).

name: Flower
reason: Cut from the coloured wildflowers; blue dye and the floral furniture use it, while standing flowers feed bees and butterflies (D24).

name: Flowstone
reason: A second decorative cave stone; one kind of rock (D22).

name: Centipede Fang
change: Rename 'Centipede Fang': from any big centipede at the bug extractor (the Centipede Cavern's giant centipedes above all); it is the blade of the Centipede-Fang Dagger.
reason: The table keeps a centipede-fang dagger past steel, and centipede fangs really are metal-hardened (P20); one fang item serves every big centipede.

name: Forest Dye
reason: A zone dye palette; single plant dyes cover colour (P11).

name: Forest Moss
reason: Its jobs were a dye, a glue and a herbal dressing, none kept; the moss clump covers the look.

name: Formic Acid
reason: What black ants give at the bug extractor (ants give formic acid, July 2026; fire ants make none); the Bug Bomb's first strength, and the gilded-steel outfit is the armour against it.

name: Formic Dab
change: Merge into formic acid
reason: A drop from each killed ant, which D18 rules out; the extractor's formic acid is the one acid.

name: Freshwater Nacre
reason: Mother-of-pearl comes from mussels, which as molluscs didn't survive (D32, D64), and its inlay and charm jobs are cut.

name: Frog Spawn
reason: Frogs are gone with the amphibians (D32).

name: Frog Toxin
reason: Frogs are gone with the amphibians (D32).

name: Fungal Spore
reason: It seeded ant fungus gardens, and our ants don't farm fungus.

name: Gem Geode
change: merge into geode (the mining find the gem cutter cracks open)
reason: A second geode doing the same job in another zone.

name: Giant Water Bug Carapace
change: merge into chitin
reason: The water bug's shell is chitin, and the diving set it plated is gone.

name: Glass
reason: Fired from sand at the furnace; the magnifying glass, terrariums, specimen cases, the telescope and clocks use it.

name: Glasswing Scale
reason: Its jobs were luck charms and prism dust, both cut.

name: Gloom Moss
reason: A glowing moss for night-sight brews; glowing mushrooms already make the night-sight potion.

name: Glow Bloom
reason: Its only job was the glow dye, which is cut, and glowing mushrooms are the plant light; glowing flowers are real, though (a gene-bred glowing petunia has been sold since 2024), so one could come back as night-garden décor.

name: Glow Crystal
reason: Crystals don't give light by themselves; light comes from bugs, torches and lamps (D49).

name: Glow Dye
reason: Dyes recolour cloth outfits by swapping colours (D44), which can't make cloth glow.

name: Glow Gland (mayfly)
change: Merge into the Glow Gland (the renamed firefly lumen)
reason: Its bug, the 'glow mayfly', is invented, and the glow gland from fireflies and glowworms does the same job.

name: Glow Sac
reason: From an invented 'glow grub', and lanterns use live bugs, not glowing gel.

name: Glow Silk
reason: A glowworm's threads are sticky snares that don't glow themselves; the glow gland covers the glowworm's material.

name: Glow Spore
reason: Glowing mushrooms already are the cave light and the night-sight base.

name: Glow Thread
reason: A glowing cloth step with no outfit that needs it.

name: Glowshroom
change: Merge into the glowing mushroom
reason: The same glowing cave mushroom under a second name.

name: Glowworm Lumen
change: Merge into the Glow Gland (the renamed firefly lumen)
reason: The glowworm's light organ does the same job as the firefly's; one glow material covers both.

name: Gold Bar
change: New jobs only: gilding (the gilded-steel outfit), connectors traded for power parts, jewelry, and selling as money. Its seven tool and weapon recipes go.
reason: Gold is too soft for tools or weapons (D49, P20), so it becomes a metal of money and machines (D61).

name: Gold Dye
reason: A 'honey gold' dye from pollen and bumblebee nectar; yellow dye covers it, and more colours come from flowers (P11).

name: Gold Ore
reason: A deep reward kept for money and machines (P20); crushed, washed, then smelted into gold bars (D26).

name: Crushed Gold Ore
change: Rename 'Crushed Gold Ore'; the step stays.
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26); 'paydirt' was a working name (D13).

name: Gorse Thorn
reason: Its jobs were thorn trinkets and trap barbs, both cut; thorn outfits use real stings.

name: Gossamer Cloth
reason: A fourth silk cloth made with an invented 'dew'; silk cloth and the spider silks cover it.

name: Gossamer Dew
reason: Dew soaked from webs to 'lighten cloth' isn't real.

name: Granite
reason: A second rock; depth shows in the floor and the ores, never in harder rock (D22).

name: Grass Turf
reason: What the shovel digs from grass and lays as grass (P12), and a compost bin input.

name: Grasshopper Leg
reason: Its jobs were springing boots and locust oil, both cut; grasshoppers give chitin and bug meat.

name: Green Dye
reason: One of the four basic dyes, made from clover and sold by the Weaver (D44).

name: Hardened Husk
reason: A made-up plate 'between plank and chitin' with no outfit or wall that needs it.

name: Hardwood
reason: Wood from the hardwood trees, which the iron axe opens (D69); used as it is for fine furniture and the forest plate outfit, the roster's outfit made of trees and plants, not bugs.

name: Hardwood Plank
reason: A second plank is an extra step; hardwood is used as it is, and ordinary planks cover building.

name: Black Ant Jaw
change: Rename 'Black Ant Jaw': from dead black ants at the bug extractor, best from older ants whose jaws have hardened (P20); it edges the Black-Ant Jaw Blade, the first bug-part sword past steel.
reason: Harvester ants are cut (D39), but the black-ant blade this table keeps needs black-ant jaws, and this is the Ant Colony's jaw item.

name: Harvestman Leg
reason: Its job was climbing gear against falls, and a world seen from above has no falls.

name: Hawk Moth Silk
reason: Hawk moths pupate in the soil with little or no silk; the emperor and luna moths are the silk moths.

name: Honeycomb
reason: What hives give; the honey extractor turns it into honey or beeswax (the player chooses, D31), and the Beekeeper buys it.

name: Honeydew
change: Collected from plants that have aphids on them, in the plant's own view (part 8), not dropped by aphids (D18); the honeydew bun takes it, and it is sweet bait for ants (P4).
reason: Ants really farm aphids for honeydew, so it ties aphids, ants and cooking together.

name: Hornet Stinger
change: Rename 'Hornet Stinger': from dead hornets at the bug extractor (their body plates are ordinary chitin); it arms the hornet-thorn outfit, the second of the three thorn outfits. The third, the killer-bee thorn, would take a killer-bee stinger the same way if killer bees join the bee line.
reason: The thorn outfits (August 2026) need each family's own sting, and a separate hornet carapace would only repeat chitin.

name: Hornet Venom
reason: The second of six venoms, from hornets at the bug extractor; stronger than wasp venom, so it makes stronger potions and a stronger Bug Bomb.

name: Spider Plate
change: Rename 'Spider Plate': the thick shell of Spider Vale East's biggest spiders (the giant huntsman and tarantulas), from their carcasses at the bug extractor; the legendary spider-plate set is built on it.
reason: The legendary spider-plate set on the outfit roster is built on spider plate, and this is the one big-spider shell in the lists.

name: Huntsman Eye
reason: Its job was a charm, which is cut.

name: Huntsman Fang
change: Merge into the Spider Fang (the renamed wolf fang)
reason: The same spider fang from a bigger spider; one fang item makes the Spider-Fang Dagger.

name: Iron Bar
reason: The fifth rung (P20): iron tools, weapons and armour, and the base of steel; the Blacksmith sells it.

name: Iron Ore
reason: Reached with the bronze pickaxe (P20); crushed, washed, then smelted (D26); bog iron folds in.

name: Crushed Iron Ore
change: Rename 'Crushed Iron Ore'; the step stays.
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26); 'paydirt' was a working name (D13).

name: Jumping Spider Eye
reason: Its job was a precision charm, which is cut.

name: Kelp Weave
reason: A wet-suit cloth for diving, which is out.

name: Ladybug Shell
change: merge into chitin
reason: Ladybugs are beetles, so their shell is chitin; red dye comes from poppies in the game, and luck charms are cut.

name: Larva Case
reason: A pebble case used as grit for pearl polishing, and pearls are cut.

name: Leaf Disc
reason: A leaf-cutter bee's leaf pieces as a fibre substitute; plain fibre covers it.

name: Bug Leather
change: Rename 'Bug Leather': made at the bug extractor from dead flies and butterflies (the owner's bug map, 2026-06-28); the bug-leather outfit, the starting armour, uses it.
reason: The name tells players this leather comes from bugs, since there are no mammal hides (D32).

name: Leech Extract
reason: No leeches (D64).

name: Lily Extract
reason: A base for calming and leech salves, both cut.

name: Litter Mulch
reason: Mulch comes from straw (P11), and leaf litter stays a plant that millipedes feed and breed on.

name: Locust Wing
reason: Its jobs were the cut locust set and lures (D10); locusts give chitin and bug meat.

name: Lotus Essence
reason: An anti-disease brew base, and there is no disease system.

name: Luminescent Thread
reason: A glowing wick and trim with no outfit or lamp that needs it; lanterns hold live bugs.

name: Luminous Resin
reason: Sap that holds light isn't real.

name: Luna Moth Dust
reason: Its jobs were a glow dye and a night-sight brew, both covered or cut.

name: Lure Resin
reason: A made-up 'mineral seep' for lures and diving gear.

name: Magma Rock
reason: A fire-zone stone; fire isn't a hazard and there is one kind of rock (D22).

name: Mantis Scythe
reason: The bug-part sickle goes to the stag beetle's jaw, and the mantis-edged weapon is cut; a mantis gives chitin and bug meat.

name: Marsh Clay
change: Merge into the clay block
reason: Clay is clay; swamp clay deposits can simply be clay blocks.

name: Boss Trophy
change: Becomes the Boss Trophy: a boss's carcass mounted for display, one kind for each boss species (the two ant queens, the queen wasp, the rhino beetle and the rest). Art on a plot (P26), and a proud piece only a hunter can own.
reason: P13 names the mounted carcass as what a boss leaves, and it gives hunters, one of the named ways to play (D67), their own décor.

name: Scorpion Shell
change: Rename 'Scorpion Shell': from dead scorpions at the bug extractor (the big brood-mother gives the most); the scorpion outfit is made from it.
reason: The owner asked for a scorpion outfit for Scorpion Rocks, and it needs the zone's own material (August 2026: outfits call for materials partly new to their zone).

name: Matron Fang
change: Merge into the Spider Fang (the renamed wolf fang)
reason: A spider boss's fang is a spider fang; its only planned job was a wall trophy.

name: Matron Forcipule
change: Merge into the Centipede Fang (the renamed forest centipede fang)
reason: A centipede boss's fang is a centipede fang; one fang item serves the dagger.

name: Mayfly Wing
reason: From an invented glowing mayfly, for trinkets and a dye that are cut.

name: Message in a Bottle
change: Reading it gives a note that points to a secret or a hidden recipe; bottles wash up along the coasts (6 placed today).
reason: Today it only sells; the game wants secrets everywhere (D53) and rare recipes hidden in the world (part 6), and a bottle on the beach is the classic way to hand one out.

name: Miasma Essence
reason: 'Miasma' is a long-disproved idea of disease, and there is no disease system.

name: Milkweed Silk
change: merge into fiber
reason: Cut milkweed gives plain fibre; milkweed floss is a real fibre, not a separate item.

name: Millipede Segment
change: merge into chitin
reason: The bug extractor already turns dead millipedes into chitin.

name: Mole Cricket Claw
reason: Its jobs were a digging pick and a drill bit, and bug parts never make pickaxes (P20).

name: Monarch Scale
reason: Its jobs were a shimmer dye and a luck brooch, both cut.

name: Mosquito Proboscis
reason: Mosquitoes carry no venom to make coatings from, and their bites are the head net's job.

name: Mosquito Venom
reason: Mosquitoes have no venom, and the fever bombs it made are cut.

name: Moth Silk
change: merge into silk
reason: Silk is moth silk already; one item for the moth line.

name: Mud
reason: Nothing makes or uses it: laying mud costs dirt and turf and digging mud gives those back, so the shovel's display should count those instead of 'mud', which nobody ever has.

name: Mud Daub
reason: A mason bee's nest mud as a drop from a bug, which D18 rules out; clay blocks cover clay.

name: Mud Dauber Clay
reason: A clay drop from a killed wasp, which D18 rules out; clay blocks cover clay.

name: Brown Mushroom
reason: The common eating mushroom (80 placed), in the village's forager stew.

name: Puffball
reason: A third eating mushroom with no recipe; the brown mushroom and the chanterelle cover eating, as for the red mushroom (3 placed).

name: Mycelium Mat
reason: Part of the ant fungus farm, and our ants don't farm fungus.

name: Nacre Inlay
reason: Mother-of-pearl comes from mussels, which as molluscs didn't survive (D32, D64), and the pearl charms it decorated are cut.

name: Nectar
reason: Bees turn nectar into honey inside the hive; nectar as an item adds nothing.

name: Nectar Bloom
reason: A bundle of flowers; the flower item and the kept nectar plants cover it.

name: Nettle Leaf
reason: It fed old cures and poison recipes that were cut or remade from venom (P16).

name: Nymph Gill
reason: A dragonfly nymph's gill with no recipe.

name: Nymph Husk
reason: Cheap filler from invented 'swarmling nymphs'; straw and compost cover mulch and filler.

name: Nymph Jaw
reason: Its job was a pole weapon, which is cut.

name: Orange
reason: Fruit from the orange trees (14 trees placed), part of the orchard's variety.

name: Orb Silk
change: Merge into spider silk
reason: Orb weavers' silk is spider silk, the middle of the three spider silks.

name: Pale Root
reason: A cave cordage plant; fibre covers cordage.

name: Paper Nest
reason: No recipe uses it, and nests are nurseries now, not loot (D23); the hornet nest, which still drops it, should become a nursery like the wasp nest.

name: Peat
reason: A second fuel and a second soil improver; coal and compost already do both jobs.

name: Peat Block
reason: A building block made from cut peat.

name: Pill Bug Chitin
change: merge into chitin
reason: Pill bugs count as bugs (D64), and their plates are chitin.

name: Plank
reason: Sawn from wood at the sawmill (the saw gives more from giant trunks, D12); furniture, floors, walls and doors, and the Carpenter sells it.

name: Platinum Bar
change: New jobs only: the platinum plate outfit (with steel bars), the metal that turns spare wind and solar power into stored hydrogen (brought to whoever builds power parts), jewelry, and selling as money. Its seven tool and weapon recipes go.
reason: Platinum is too soft and heavy for tools (P20), and D61 gives it fancy armour, money and machines instead.

name: Platinum Ore
reason: A deep reward kept for money and machines (P20); crushed, washed, then smelted (D26).

name: Crushed Platinum Ore
change: Rename 'Crushed Platinum Ore'; the step stays.
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26); 'paydirt' was a working name (D13).

name: Plum
reason: Fruit from the plum trees (30 trees placed), part of the orchard's variety.

name: Pollen
change: Comes from beehives now and then (beekeepers really trap pollen at the hive door), not dropped by bees (D18); the pollen patty hive feed takes it.
reason: It gives the hive a second product and feeds the kept hive feed.

name: Pollen Dye
reason: A second yellow dye; the dandelion's yellow dye covers it.

name: Pond Clay
change: Merge into the clay block
reason: D19 already folded it into plain clay.

name: Centipede Matron Venom
change: Keep as the Centipede Cavern boss's own part: only her carcass gives it; the strongest centipede antivenom and a recipe from the Ecologist's quests (P9, P13).
reason: P13 says a boss's carcass gives materials only a boss gives; many centipedes keep growing all their lives, so the oldest really are the biggest.

name: Scorpion Matron Venom
change: Keep as the Scorpion Rocks boss's own part (the biggest female of the zone's real scorpion species): only her carcass gives it; the strongest scorpion antivenom and a recipe from the Ecologist's quests (P9, P13).
reason: P13 promises boss-only materials; the huntsman spider's share goes to spider venom as the table says.

name: Pressed Apple
reason: A half-made cider step; the press turns fruit straight into juice (P11).

name: Prime Carapace
change: merge into chitin
reason: The rhino beetle's shell is ordinary beetle chitin; its boss-only part is the great horn (the Rhino-Horn Maul), as P13 wants.

name: Prism Dust
reason: Grit for prism goggles and gem-luck charms, both cut.

name: Propolis
reason: The honey bandage is made from honey, and nothing else needs bee glue.

name: Pumpkin
reason: A village vegetable, the big single harvest, in the hearty stew and the roast.

name: Quartz
reason: The common gem mineral from quartz deposits and the crystal clusters (crystal folds in); the gem cutter cuts it to sell or set in jewelry.

name: Black Ant Queen Chitin
change: Rename 'Black Ant Queen Chitin': from the black-ant queen, the Ant Colony's mini-boss, at the bug extractor; half of what the legendary queens' set needs, with the fire-ant queen's chitin and rare metals.
reason: The owner's queens' set needs parts from both colony queens, which sends players across the whole underground.

name: Queen Venom
reason: Ants give formic acid at the extractor (July 2026), and black widow venom is already the top venom; the queen's part with a job is her chitin.

name: Raw Emerald
change: merge into emerald
reason: The emerald item already is the raw gem, mined from emerald deposits.

name: Raw Gem
reason: A mystery gem that the geode already covers.

name: Raw Sapphire
change: merge into sapphire
reason: The sapphire item already is the raw gem.

name: Reaper Chitin
change: merge into chitin
reason: The mantis's shell is chitin; the locust-warden armour it capped is cut (D10).

name: Red Dye
reason: One of the four basic dyes, made from poppies and sold by the Weaver (D44).

name: Reed Fiber
change: merge into fiber
reason: D15 folds reed fibre into plain fibre.

name: Reed Stalk
change: merge into fiber
reason: Reeds drop plain fibre (D15), and thatch roofs are out (D19).

name: Washed Copper Ore
change: Rename 'Washed Copper Ore' (the sluice's output); smelted with coal into copper bars.
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26), and the name should say which step made it.

name: Washed Gold Ore
change: Rename 'Washed Gold Ore'; smelted into gold bars.
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26).

name: Washed Iron Ore
change: Rename 'Washed Iron Ore'; smelted into iron bars.
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26).

name: Washed Platinum Ore
change: Rename 'Washed Platinum Ore'; smelted into platinum bars.
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26).

name: Refined Silk
reason: A second spinning step with an invented 'silk gland' ingredient, an extra realistic step (D42); silk goes straight to the loom.

name: Washed Silver Ore
change: Rename 'Washed Silver Ore'; smelted into silver bars.
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26).

name: Washed Tin Ore
change: Rename 'Washed Tin Ore'; it goes straight into bronze with copper bars at the forge (no tin bar).
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26), and tin's only job is bronze.

name: Resin Glob
change: Merge into tree resin
reason: Tree resin is the same sticky sap; one resin item serves the venom coating.

name: Rhino Beetle Horn
change: The rhino-beetle boss's own part (P13), from its carcass at the bug extractor; the head of the Rhino-Horn Maul.
reason: P13 promises each boss a material of its own, and the tank's top weapon needs it.

name: River Pebble
reason: D19 cut it from the village; stone covers paths.

name: River Reed
change: merge into fiber
reason: Reeds give plain fibre (D15).

name: River Silt
reason: A dredged silt for a special brick; dredging is a backlog idea (D14) and brick is made from clay.

name: Salt
change: Rename 'Salt': mined as rock salt in Scorpion Rocks and sold at the general store so village cooks have it; the bug jerky and the crayfish boil take it. Cave salt folds in.
reason: Two kept meals need salt, and one plain salt item is enough.

name: Rotten Fruit
change: Becomes the one 'Rotten Fruit': every fallen fruit rots into it; flies feed and breed on it, it is fly bait in a dish (P4) and goes into compost. The rotten cherry, orange and plum merge in.
reason: Four rotten fruits do exactly the same job, so one item is simpler for bait, compost and the flies.

name: Rotten Cherry
change: Merge into Rotten Fruit (the renamed rotten apple)
reason: The same fly food and bait as every other rotten fruit.

name: Rotten Orange
change: Merge into Rotten Fruit (the renamed rotten apple)
reason: The same fly food and bait as every other rotten fruit.

name: Rotten Plum
change: Merge into Rotten Fruit (the renamed rotten apple)
reason: The same fly food and bait as every other rotten fruit.

name: Royal Jelly
change: Comes from beehives, rarely (beekeepers really take it from the cells where queens are raised), not from sweat bees, the fire-ant queen or a pile on the ground; the strong healing potion and the royal jelly meal take it.
reason: Royal jelly is a signature bee product, and only bees make it.

name: Ant Royal Jelly
reason: Ants don't make royal jelly; the bees' royal jelly is the one.

name: Royal Pheromone
reason: Ant trail scent comes from workers, not the queen; the Ant Trail Scent (kept for later) can be made straight from ant carcasses, as the colony-scent pouch is.

name: Royal Silk
reason: Huntsman spiders hunt without webs; black widow silk is the top silk.

name: Royal Silk Cloth
reason: A second top cloth; the widow's armour takes black widow silk directly.

name: Queen Wasp Venom
change: Keep as the queen wasp's own part: only her carcass gives it at the bug extractor; it makes the strongest wasp antivenom and goes into a recipe from the Ecologist's quests (P9, P13).
reason: P13 promises boss-only materials, and the table otherwise leaves only the two ant queens with one.

name: Royal Wax
reason: A 'premium' second wax; beeswax covers candles and the salve.

name: Ruby
reason: A gem mined from ruby deposits; it sells and cuts into a jewelry stone.

name: Saltpeter
reason: Its job was gunpowder for dynamite, which isn't designed; salt covers curing food.

name: Sand
change: Merge into the sand block: the sand block gives itself when dug (D22), glass is fired from it, and the shovel lays it as sand ground.
reason: Today a dug sand block turns into 'sand' and can never be placed as a block again; one sand item fixes that.

name: Sandstone
reason: A second kind of rock (D22), and the sandstone block it would fold into is cut too.

name: Sapphire
reason: A gem mined from sapphire deposits; it sells and cuts into a jewelry stone.

name: Scorched Clay
reason: A 'fire-hardened' clay for invented ramparts; clay blocks and bricks cover it.

name: Scorpion Brood
reason: Young are taken from a nursery, not dropped by a boss (D18, D23).

name: Scorpion Sting
change: Rename 'Scorpion Sting': the sting tip, from dead scorpions at the bug extractor; it tips the Scorpion-Sting Spear, the top spear past steel. A scorpion's claws are ordinary chitin.
reason: The table keeps a scorpion-sting spear (a scorpion's sting tip is up to a quarter zinc, P20), and claws have no job of their own.

name: Scorpion Venom
reason: The fourth of six venoms, from scorpions at the bug extractor; the classic real antivenom source, making a strong antivenom and coating (P16).

name: Seashell
reason: Old shells washed up on the coasts are remains, which the premise allows (D66); beachcombing on the coasts pays a little.

name: Seed Husk
reason: Granary chaff from harvester ants, which are cut.

name: Serpent Glow Cap
reason: Named after serpents (gone), and glowing mushrooms already cover cave light.

name: Serpentfly Ichor
reason: The 'bog serpent fly' is invented (D39).

name: Serpentfly Scale
reason: The 'bog serpent fly' is invented (D39).

name: Shimmer Dye
reason: Dyes recolour cloth outfits by swapping colours (D44), which can't make a shimmer.

name: Silk
change: Becomes the one moth silk: from the cocoons of wild silk moths (emperor and luna moths) in the Butterfly Fields, taken from their nursery at the cocoon stage; the loom weaves it into silk cloth. Moth silk and emperor silk merge in.
reason: It exists in the game with no source or use; moth cocoons are where real silk comes from, which makes silk a product of bug farming.

name: Silk Cloth
reason: Woven from silk at the loom; fine furniture and fine clothes such as the decorative outfits.

name: Silk Gland
reason: An ingredient for a second silk-spinning step, which the game skips (D42).

name: Silk Resin
reason: An invented 'burrow secretion' sealant.

name: Wild Silk Thread
reason: Butterflies form a bare chrysalis, not a silk cocoon, so cabbage whites give no silk.

name: Silt Block
reason: A special brick from dredged silt; clay brick covers building.

name: Silt Brick
reason: A special brick from dredged silt and peat; clay brick covers building.

name: Silver Bar
change: New jobs only: solar panels, contacts and mirrors (brought to whoever builds power parts), jewelry, and selling as money. Its seven tool and weapon recipes go.
reason: Silver is softer than bronze, so it leaves the tools (P20) and becomes a metal of money and machines (D61).

name: Silver Ore
reason: A deep reward kept for money and machines (P20); crushed, washed, then smelted (D26).

name: Crushed Silver Ore
change: Rename 'Crushed Silver Ore'; the step stays.
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26); 'paydirt' was a working name (D13).

name: Silverfish Scale
reason: A combat drop with no recipe.

name: Pond Skater Oil
reason: It was for walking on water, which is out: shallow water is waded, deep water takes a boat (D51).

name: Snail Shell
reason: It dropped from living snails, which are gone (D64); old shells are the seashell's job.

name: Soft Stone
reason: A second rock; one kind of rock (D22).

name: Fire Ant Chitin
change: Rename 'Fire Ant Chitin': from dead fire ants (soldiers above all) at the bug extractor in the Deadly Ants zone; the approved fire-ant outfit is made from it.
reason: The fire-ant outfit is one of the four finished outfits, and outfits call for materials from their own zone (August 2026).

name: Black Ant Chitin
change: Rename 'Black Ant Chitin': from dead black ants (soldiers above all) at the bug extractor in the Ant Colony; the approved black-ant outfit is made from it.
reason: The black-ant outfit is one of the four finished outfits; soldier ants are black ants with a job, not a species of their own (D39).

name: Spider Egg Sac
reason: Young are taken from a nursery, not dropped by a boss (D23).

name: Spider Silk
change: Its sources become spiders at the bug extractor and webs cut with a blade (D12); it is the middle of the three spider silks, for the silk outfit of Spider Vale West. Orb silk, broodmother silk, trapdoor silk and cobweb merge in.
reason: The stealth outfits climb cave spider, spider, black widow (the outfit roster), and the old source, the 'web tender', is invented.

name: Spider Silk Cloth
reason: The silk outfits take spider silk directly; a cloth step in between adds nothing (D42).

name: Spider Venom
reason: The fifth of six venoms, from spiders at the bug extractor; a stronger spider gives a stronger antivenom.

name: Spiderling Cluster
reason: The 'spiderling swarm' is invented (D39).

name: Springtail Dust
reason: A third glow powder; the glow gland covers glow.

name: Spun Silk
reason: An extra spinning step between silk and cloth (D42); the loom weaves silk directly.

name: Stag Beetle Jaw
change: Rename 'Stag Beetle Jaw' (it is a beetle's jaw, not a deer's antler): from dead stag beetles at the bug extractor in the Millipede Forest; it is the blade of the Mandible Sickle.
reason: The bug-part sickle is made from a stag beetle's jaw, and the old name read as a mammal part.

name: Starfish
reason: A starfish reads as a living sea animal, and only bugs, fish and people survive (D32); its 21 placements can become seashell piles.

name: Steel Bar
reason: The sixth rung (P20): iron bars and coal at the forge; the top metal weapons, and the base of cobalt steel, tungsten steel, the platinum plate and the gilded-steel outfit; the Blacksmith sells it.

name: Stone
change: Merge into the stone block: digging stone and cave floors gives stone blocks, and stone paths and floors are laid from them.
reason: Mining gives 'stone block' but only 'stone' lays paths, so a miner with a full bag of stone can't pave anything; one rock, one item (D22).

name: Water Strider Leg
reason: It was for walking on water, which is out (D51).

name: Water Strider Oil
reason: Waterproofing for diving gear, which is out.

name: Sunflower Seed
reason: Harvesting a sunflower gives its seeds, which also replant it.

name: Sunken Log
reason: Raised by diving or dredging for a special swamp plank; wood and hardwood cover building.

name: Swamp Dye
reason: A zone dye palette; single plant dyes cover colour (P11).

name: Swamp Gas
reason: Lamp fuel and gas bombs; there are no oil or gas lamps (D49), and there are no gas dangers (D43).

name: Swamp Lotus
reason: Gathered by diving for anti-disease brews, and neither diving nor disease is in the game.

name: Swarm Essence
reason: A pheromone charge for the swarm culler and swarm lures, both cut.

name: Tanned Hide
reason: Hide comes from mammals (gone, D32), and tanning is an extra realistic step (D42); bug leather covers leather.

name: Tanned Leather
reason: The same mammal-leather idea; bug leather covers leather.

name: Tannin
reason: Its only job was tanning hides, which are gone.

name: Tarantula Hair
reason: Its jobs were an itching-powder weapon and thorn lining, both cut; tarantulas give spider plate.

name: Thatch
reason: Roofing, and there are no roofs (D19).

name: Thistle Down
reason: Stuffing and tinder with no recipe; fibre covers stuffing.

name: Thread
reason: Spun from fibre on the spinning wheel (P11) and woven into cloth; the Weaver sells it.

name: Tick Sac
reason: Its jobs were a life-stealing coating and the old tick repellent; the tick repellent needs no tick parts.

name: Timber Snail Shell
reason: It dropped from a living snail, and snails are gone (D64); old shells are the seashell's job.

name: Tin Ore
reason: Reached with the copper pickaxe (P20); crushed and washed, it goes into bronze.

name: Crushed Tin Ore
change: Rename 'Crushed Tin Ore'; the step stays.
reason: Crush, wash, smelt is the owner's chain (D26); 'paydirt' was a working name (D13).

name: Tomato
reason: A village vegetable with several harvests (170 plants placed).

name: Trapdoor Lid
reason: A rare décor drop with no job; trapdoor spiders give spider silk.

name: Trapdoor Silk
change: Merge into spider silk
reason: Trapdoor spiders' silk is spider silk.

name: Tree Resin
change: Chopping pine trees sometimes gives it, anywhere pines grow (not only the Millipede Forest); the venom coating is made from a bug's venom and resin. Resin glob folds in.
reason: The venom coating needs resin, and pine resin is real and common (1,846 pines placed).

name: Venom
reason: A generic venom names no bug; each of the six kept venoms names the bug it comes from, so stronger bugs make stronger potions (P16).

name: Wasp Venom
change: Rename 'Wasp Venom': from dead wasps at the bug extractor; the first and mildest of six venoms (wasp, hornet, centipede, scorpion, spider, black widow), making the first antivenom, venom resistance and venom coating (P16). Royal venom folds in.
reason: Wasp stings are the antivenom's first strength, and the name should say where the venom comes from.

name: Vinegaroon Acid
reason: Its jobs were a gem-cutting etch and an armour-shredding throw; the gem cutter needs nothing extra, and formic acid is the one acid.

name: Fire Ant Queen Chitin
change: Rename 'Fire Ant Queen Chitin': from the fire-ant queen at the heart of the Deadly Ants zone, at the bug extractor; the other half of the legendary queens' set.
reason: The owner's queens' set needs parts from both colony queens.

name: Wasp Larvae
reason: What the wasp nest gives when you take its brood (built), and what you place in another nest to start or top it up (D23).

name: Wasp Stinger
change: Its source becomes dead wasps at the bug extractor (the direct drop was removed, D22); its job is the wasp-thorn outfit, the first of the three thorn outfits. The smoker's recipe uses one today and could take bug leather for the bellows instead.
reason: The thorn outfits (August 2026) sting whoever hits the wearer, so each needs its family's real sting.

name: Water Beetle Shell
change: merge into chitin
reason: A diving beetle's shell is beetle chitin; the diving helmet it lined is gone.

name: Water Bug Venom Gland
reason: A seventh venom for one swamp boss; the antivenom still cures its bite, and six venoms cover the potion strengths.

name: Black Widow Silk
change: Rename 'Black Widow Silk': from black widows at the bug extractor or cut from their webs, in Spider Vale East; the widow's armour, the top stealth outfit, is made from it.
reason: The stealth outfits end in the widow's armour (outfit roster), and black widow silk is famously strong.

name: Wheat
reason: The Locust Farmland's crop (D42); the mill turns it into flour, and cutting it down gives straw.

name: Whirligig Shell
change: merge into chitin
reason: A whirligig beetle's shell is beetle chitin.

name: Black Widow Venom
reason: The strongest of the six venoms, from black widows in Spider Vale East; it makes the strongest antivenom and the strongest Bug Bomb.

name: Spider Fang
change: Rename 'Spider Fang': from the big spiders of Spider Vale at the bug extractor; it is the blade of the Spider-Fang Dagger, the top dagger. Huntsman and matron fangs merge in.
reason: The table keeps one spider-fang dagger, and 'wolf fang' read as a mammal's tooth.

name: Wood
reason: Chopped from trees everywhere; planks, torches, tool handles and early building, and the furnace burns it into coal.

name: Yellow Dye
reason: One of the four basic dyes, made from dandelions and sold by the Weaver (D44).

name: Cobalt Ore
change: A new ore mined with the steel pickaxe in the deep rock zones, often beside silver; its examine text tells how its pink crust ('cobalt bloom') led real prospectors to silver. Crushed and washed like every ore (D26), it goes into cobalt steel.
reason: Every pickaxe rung must open an ore (P20), and cobalt is one of the two new ores the owner accepted (D61).

name: Crushed Cobalt Ore
change: The rock crusher's output for cobalt ore; washed at the sluice next.
reason: Every ore is crushed, washed, then smelted (D26).

name: Washed Cobalt Ore
change: The sluice's output for cobalt; the forge adds it to steel bars to make cobalt steel bars, the way washed tin joins copper bars to make bronze (no plain cobalt bar).
reason: Every ore is crushed, washed, then smelted (D26), and cobalt's only job is mixing into steel.

name: Cobalt Steel Bar
change: Made at the forge from steel bars and washed cobalt ore; the seventh tool rung and the top rung of metal armour (the cobalt-steel pickaxe and outfit).
reason: P20 and D61 put cobalt steel on the seventh rung, and armour stops there.

name: Tungsten Ore
change: Mined with the cobalt-steel pickaxe in the deepest rock; it glows sky-blue under the UV lamp, as the real ore scheelite does. Crushed and washed, it goes into tungsten steel.
reason: The eighth rung needs its ore (P20), and its glow gives the UV lamp its job.

name: Crushed Tungsten Ore
change: The rock crusher's output for tungsten ore; washed at the sluice next.
reason: Every ore is crushed, washed, then smelted (D26).

name: Washed Tungsten Ore
change: The sluice's output for tungsten; the forge adds it to steel bars to make tungsten steel bars, the way cobalt makes cobalt steel (no plain tungsten bar).
reason: Every ore is crushed, washed, then smelted (D26), and tungsten's job is mixing into steel (D69).

name: Tungsten Steel Bar
change: Made at the forge from steel bars and washed tungsten ore; the eighth tool rung (the tungsten-steel pickaxe) and the rock drill's bits.
reason: The top tool rung is tungsten steel (D61, renamed in D69).

name: Cotton
change: A later crop grown outside the village (for example in the Locust Farmland); the spinning wheel spins it into thread, a second cloth source beside plant fibre and silk. Its plant and seed come with the crops.
reason: D15 decided to add cotton as a cloth source, a later crop and not in the village, and no item exists for it.

name: Netting
reason: One woven mesh is enough: the fly netting (fine netting) and the heavy netting are what net runs are strung from, woven at the loom in one step, and the cast net is woven from cord.

name: Bone Meal
change: The mill grinds bones into bone meal in one step, a fertiliser that raises yield (D42); how strong it is next to compost is set with the fertiliser design (section 06).
reason: It gives bones, the one kept remains that drop an item, a real use, as Stardew's bone mill does, and uses the mill P11 already plans.

name: Anchor
reason: An old ship's anchor is a salvaged relic that suits a dock or a fisher's plot; it has its own look and stands twice in the village.

name: Ant Colony Chart
change: Needs its sprite (it has none).
reason: A chart of an ant colony's castes is bug-science décor for the myrmecologist's building and an ant keeper's home, the game's own kind of art; it stands in the Ant Tunnels.

name: Ant Eggs
change: Becomes the egg stage of an ant colony's brood, shown in the nest's panel and taken or moved like fly and wasp eggs; the loose pick-up (which gives an 'Ant Egg' item) goes.
reason: Ants lay eggs rather than drop them (D18), and ranching ants (D67) needs ant brood to work like every other nursery.

name: Antenna
reason: Nothing in the game receives a signal, so it has no job; the weather board covers forecasts. Unplaced.

name: Anvil
change: Makes every metal tool, weapon and armour rung, copper to tungsten steel; the tools, weapons and armour the forge makes today move here. Stays in the blacksmith's smithy in the village, usable and not takeable (D55).
reason: Anvil and forge both make tools today, split by tier for no reason a player can see; one station for metal gear is clearer.

name: Apple Crate
change: Stays as market and orchard dressing (a townsperson's crate of apples) but can't be broken for apples and wood.
reason: All ten stand in the village, where players can't break or take the townspeople's things (D41); apples come from the orchard.

name: Aquarium
reason: A fish tank suits a player who fishes, and fishing starts in the village (D51); a distinct piece, placed once in the village.

name: Armchair
reason: The living-room armchair, crafted at the sawmill; placed in the village and the Bee Meadow.

name: Wingback Armchair
reason: The fancy armchair, part of the bought-later fancy set (D19); three stand in the village.

name: Autonet
change: Give it the accepted job: it draws in bugs from the area just ahead of it, holds more than a net run and stops when full, and the player empties it by hand (P3). Today it only stores items.
reason: The autonet is the decided machine catcher (D34), but in the prototype it is a plain storage box.

name: Awning
reason: A cloth awning gives shopfronts, stalls and players' houses character for little cost; the weaver's cloth goods.

name: Bait Basket
reason: Its picture is a basket of worms, and there are no worms (D64); the bait dish covers bait. Unplaced.

name: Bait Station
change: Becomes the Bait Dish (P4): a dish on a short post that holds one bait, such as rotting fruit for flies, a carcass for carrion beetles or something sweet for wasps (bees come too), and draws the species that like it from nearby to a catcher beside it.
reason: Bait in a dish beside a catcher is the accepted design (P4), and its picture is already a dish on a post; two stand in the Ant Tunnels.

name: Bar Cart
reason: A drinks trolley repeats the wine rack while drinks don't exist yet; unplaced filler.

name: Barrel
change: Give it a workbench recipe (wood); it has none today.
reason: Cheap storage and the most used town prop (34 placed), a second look beside the crate; no one can make or buy it yet.

name: Basket
reason: A small lidded store (D27), cheap and early; placed in the village and the Bee Meadow.

name: Bathtub
reason: A bathroom is its own kind of room, and this is its piece; four stand in the village.

name: Beach Umbrella
reason: World-only, unplaced and without a job; docks, boats and nets dress the coast.

name: Basic Bed
reason: The first bed: sleeping in it sets where you wake, and players may sleep only in their own or an abandoned bed (D45).

name: Canopy Bed
reason: A second premium bed doing the same job as the fancy bed; unplaced. Its recipe slot at the carpenter's passes to the four-poster bed.

name: Fancy Bed
change: Rename 'Four-Poster Bed' (its picture has four tall posts); the one premium bed, its recipe sold by the carpenter in the canopy bed's place.
reason: One fancy bed is enough, and this one already stands three times (village and Bee Meadow).

name: Floral Bed
reason: Part of the floral set, eight pieces that repeat the basic furniture with flowers painted on; no one sells the set, none is placed and none has a sprite.

name: Stone Slab Bed
reason: A stone copy of the bed; unplaced and without a sprite.

name: Large Bee Station
change: Needs its sprite (it has none).
reason: One of the two hive boxes the owner chose when the four hive sizes were collapsed (2026-07-06); Maren sells it.

name: Small Bee Station
change: Needs its sprite (it has none).
reason: The other hive box the owner kept (2026-07-06); Maren sells it and four stand in her apiary.

name: Bee Waterer
change: Merge into the Butterfly Water Dish (the birdbath's new form); its shallow pebble-and-water tub is the right picture for that dish, and bees drink from it too.
reason: Two water dishes for pollinators would be one job twice; the one in Maren's apiary becomes the dish.

name: Basic Beehive
reason: The owner replaced the hive tiers with the two bee stations (2026-07-06); the four in the village never come alive, and become small bee stations.

name: Deluxe Beehive
reason: Replaced by the large bee station (2026-07-06); unplaced.

name: Large Beehive
reason: Replaced by the bee stations (2026-07-06); unplaced.

name: Medium Beehive
reason: Replaced by the bee stations (2026-07-06); unplaced.

name: Maren (Beekeeper)
reason: The Bee Meadow's townsperson and the heart of the honey trade: she sells the bee stations, smoker, suit and calm spray and buys honey, comb and wax.

name: Beetle Eggs
reason: The carrion beetle's egg stage in its nursery, shown in the panel and taken or moved like other brood.

name: Beetle Grubs
reason: The carrion beetle's grub stage in its nursery.

name: Beetle Pupae
reason: The carrion beetle's pupa stage in its nursery.

name: Wooden Bench
reason: The town's outdoor seat (ten placed), an early craft at the workbench.

name: Marble Bench
